answer: Random-walk scoring curbs Sybil attacks in an agent economy by treating each identity as a vertex in an endorsement graph with a hollow adjacency matrix that blocks self-vouching. Auditors iterate a short-step Markov transition kernel from trusted seeds and admit only accounts above a floor, bounding leaked trust by the attack-edge cut. Adding fake nodes dilutes that flow, forcing attackers to acquire costly peer endorsements per identity. Yet honest newcomers with sparse links risk exclusion.
